Link Connected Searching Not MAVLink

Nothing is transmitting on that wire.

Tried 57 600, 115 200, 230 400 and 921 600. No bytes arrived at any of them — not even malformed ones, which is what a wrong speed looks like.

Check pin 8 to the autopilot's RX, pin 10 to its TX, and a shared ground on pin 6. A swapped pair looks exactly like this.

Something is transmitting, but it isn't MAVLink.

Bytes arrived at all four speeds and not one of them formed a valid frame. So something is reaching the receive pin. Its port may be set to another protocol, or to a rate outside the four. A wiring fault that corrupts rather than silences — a poor ground, an intermittent joint — looks like this too, and nothing here has exercised the transmit wire.

The autopilot's port is most likely set to a protocol other than MAVLink, or to a speed outside the four. Check its SERIALn_PROTOCOL and SERIALn_BAUD for whichever port you wired.

Anyone who can reach this board could command the aircraft.

MAVLink carries no password. Opened to the network, every device on every network Yonder is joined to — the mobile network and the mesh included — can arm it, change its flight mode and write its parameters, with no credential at all.

The autopilot still checks every command, and Yonder still logs each one. Neither of those is authentication.
